summary: The worker prompt's mandated first command, eval "$(scripts/fsgg-coord whoami --mint)", is refused outright inside a worktree-isolated agent: the harness rejects it as 'too complex to verify that it stays inside the worktree' and tells the agent to break it into plain separate commands.
evidence: command:scripts/fsgg-coord whoami --mint (run plainly, then FSGG_WORKER exported per invocation); the eval form returned a harness refusal instead of executing
cost: one refused command plus one retry; identity was still minted correctly on the second attempt

summary: The fsgg-sdd lifecycle was deliberately not used: rogue3#15 is a Class:hardening, Severity:Medium board item whose whole deliverable is one checker script, one exceptions ledger and one workflow, and the worker envelope routes S/M effort to direct implementation.
evidence: issue:EHotwagner/rogue3#15 (Paths: .github/workflows/, scripts/ ; Class: hardening); command:scripts/fsgg-coord ready --repo rogue3 --json reports class hardening severity Medium and no work/<id> charter exists for this item

summary: Building a --selftest into the checker before trusting it caught a real defect in the checker itself: --grandfather rebuilt the ledger from violations only, so a second run reclassified already-excused bindings as excused-not-violating and wrote an EMPTY ledger, silently un-excusing everything.
evidence: command:python3 scripts/check-audit-bindings.py --selftest (19 checks; the case 'the ledger is byte-stable across reruns' failed before the fix and passes after); file:scripts/check-audit-bindings.py (grandfather now seeds entries from result['excusedEntries'] before appending current violations)
cost: none avoidable; the defect was found and fixed inside the first implementation loop rather than after merge
owner: rogue3/scripts (the pattern generalises: a repo-hardening checker that gates other work should gate itself first)

summary: Audit-binding staleness has grown since it was first measured: at 1f19809 all 13 of 13 cycle audits carry at least one stale binding, 45 of 118 unique file bindings are stale, versus the 11-of-12 and 51 raw digests recorded at 97a352a. Every merged cycle report in the repository currently fails its own evidence binding.
evidence: command:python3 scripts/check-audit-bindings.py (exit 1: '13 audits, 118 bindings, 73 fresh' with 45 stale bindings listed per audit); file:feedback/2026-08-01-Rogue3-12.md; file:feedback/2026-08-02-Rogue3.md
cost: none in this cycle; the pre-existing 45 had to be excused as a baseline because rebinding an accepted audit would pin bytes its critic never read
owner: rogue3/feedback (audit rebinding policy) and .agents/skills/fs-gg-feedback-report (the skill mints the digests but nothing re-checks them after merge)

summary: A board item's declared Paths cannot cover the work the worker envelope mandates: item 15 declares 'Paths: .github/workflows/, scripts/', yet the same envelope requires committing feedback/<report>.md, feedback/audits/<report>.audit.json and feedback/checkpoints/<cycle>.jsonl. Every worker in a disjoint-path fan-out necessarily writes outside its declared paths, into a directory all three lanes share.
cost: none this cycle - the shared writes are to per-worker filenames assigned in advance, which is what prevents the collision rather than the path declaration
owner: rogue3/board item template and .agents/skills/pnext-item (Paths field semantics vs mandatory feedback artifacts)

summary: The remedy the audit-binding check names first, 'rebind the audit', has no command behind it: feedback-tool.fsx offers checkpoint, activate, digest, validate, validate-checkpoints and validate-checkpoint-state, but nothing that recomputes an existing audit's evidence digests. Rebinding means hand-editing every sha256 in the JSON.
evidence: command:dotnet fsi .agents/skills/fs-gg-feedback-report/scripts/feedback-tool.fsx -- (usage lists six subcommands, none of which rebinds); file:.agents/skills/fs-gg-feedback-report/SKILL.md
cost: this is why the 45 pre-existing stale bindings were excused as a baseline rather than rebound; rebinding 45 digests across 13 audits by hand was not a supported operation

summary: An independent review found five false-negative bypasses in a gate whose entire purpose is preventing false negatives: an unresolvable or absolute file: locator was silently skipped, a file:../ locator digested a file outside the repository and called it fresh, a non-UTF-8 bound file crashed the checker AND its own --grandfather escape hatch with an uncaught UnicodeDecodeError, a structurally mangled audit contributed zero bindings and passed, and documented exit code 2 was never returned.
evidence: command:python3 scripts/check-audit-bindings.py --selftest (19 cases before review, 53 after; the new cases cover escaping locators, BOM/CR/CRLF against a golden vector produced by the F# tool, non-UTF-8 files, malformed audit shape, and every documented exit code); issue:EHotwagner/rogue3#27
cost: one review round and roughly 35 minutes of rework, all before merge; the 19-case self-test that had already caught one defect was thorough about the happy path and blind to malformed input
owner: rogue3/scripts - and generally: a self-test written by the author of the thing it tests inherits the author's blind spots, so an adversarial reader is not redundant with it
